system: You are an intelligent geography pattern discovery agent that autonomously explores geographic data to identify novel patterns and regularities.
region_name: San Francisco Bay Area hillslopes, California

data_description.dataset_name: SPL4SMGP.008 SMAP L4 Global 3-hourly 9-km Surface and Root Zone Soil Moisture

spatial_coverage.region_name: San Francisco Bay Area hillslopes, California
spatial_coverage.coverage: Shallow-landslide-prone hillslopes of the East Bay Hills and surrounding San Francisco Bay Area catchments, California, within the global SMAP L4 land footprint between about 85°S and 85°N.

data_description.spatial_resolution: 9 km EASE-Grid, reprojected to about 11 km in Earth Engine
analytical_capabilities: Track surface and root-zone soil moisture at sub-daily resolution
Compare surface, root-zone, and total-profile moisture states across depths
Resolve wetting and drying sequences within individual storm events
Relate soil-moisture state to terrain, land cover, or hazard-susceptibility layers
Aggregate sub-daily fields to daily, seasonal, or catchment-mean summaries

unit_of_measurement.primary_measurement: Volumetric soil moisture as a volume fraction (m3/m3); wetness bands dimensionless; temperature bands in kelvin
unit_of_measurement.runtime_hint: Use `sm_surface` for the 0-5 cm layer, `sm_rootzone` for 0-100 cm, and `sm_profile` for the full column to model bedrock depth, all as volume fractions; `sm_surface_wetness` and `sm_rootzone_wetness` are the same layers expressed as dimensionless wetness. Images arrive every 3 hours, so aggregate before comparing against daily or event-scale variables. Divide by soil porosity if degree of saturation is needed.

data_description.data_source: NASA National Snow and Ice Data Center; the product assimilates SMAP L-band brightness temperature into the GEOS-5 Catchment land-surface model
data_description.region_scope_provenance: paper_ideas/single_dataset/task_005.json research_question names 旧金山湾区浅层滑坡易发坡地; seed full text (10.1029/2019WR025577) narrows this to the East Bay Hills, Alameda County, with 10 monitored catchments
